Brady Update: State Judge Rules That Prop. 215 Does Not Apply, Even In A California Court;
Subjects Brady To Random Testing By The Same Police Who Are Trying To Railroad Him!

By Richard Cowan

The ordeal of cannabis writer Pete Brady keeps getting both weirder and worse.

Brady suffers from chronic pain from a serious back injury for which he has had surgery, and from recurring depression, aggravated by the pain -- and now by the police.

As you may recall, Brady was caught up in the Butte County war on medical marijuana activist and Libertarian candidate for California governor, Steve Kubby.

Police saw Brady visiting Kubby when he was taking pictures of Kubby’s plants for an article, and somehow decided that Brady, who is white and has short hair, was a Rastafarian ganja smuggler. Remember, these are the Keystone narcs we are talking about here.
See
Tahoe Paper Carries Front Page Article Laying Out The Battle Lines In The Kubby Case:
"We think this will be the ‘Scopes Monkey Trial’ of medical marijuana," said Steve Kubby.
"This entire clash of cultures and ideology will be on the table."

They have subsequently admitted that they have no evidence that Brady was carrying even a gram when he left the Kubbys.
See
Prosecutor Admits To Washington Times That They Do Not Know
Whether Pete Brady Carried Any Marijuana When He Left The Kubbys.
Amazing Admission In An Odd Place.
But that didn’t stop police from storming into Brady’s home two days after Kubby’s arrest,  claiming to be there on a "routine" probation check. They found his medical marijuana, and laughed at his doctor’s recommendation for it; they also allege that they found some small illegal cacti.  Brady is on state probation for small scale pre-Prop 215 medical marijuana growing – not for sales.  

This was on the last day of his probation from that charge, and now they are threatening to revoke that probation and send him to prison for over 3 years, for acting on his Prop 215 rights!

Their behavior toward Brady and the fact they have not dropped conspiracy charges against the Kubbys, even after admitting that they have no evidence of sales, can be interpreted in two ways.

  1. They hope to extort testimony against the Kubbys from Brady.
  2. They are waging a vendetta against Brady for having written articles in High Times critical of Butte county law enforcement’s war on medical marijuana users.

Of course, the two are not mutually exclusive. It may well be both. Police have re-visited Brady’s home on at least two occasions, the only possible purpose being to intimidate him. Also police and prosecutors have made comments to reporters indicating that they are targeting Brady in part because he worked for High Times.

In any case, when Brady appeared in Butte County Superior Court on Monday, February 22, Butte County Deputy District Attorney Claire Keithley stunned observers by demanding that Brady be remanded into custody unless he agreed to submit to random in-home urine tests and searches as a condition of his bail release. If Brady tested dirty for his medicine, or if any was found in his home, his $12,000 bail would be revoked.

When a federal judge put similar conditions on medical marijuana activist Todd McCormick and writer Peter McWilliams, threatening to forfeit their bail, people were indignant but not surprised.
See
Peter McWilliams On Non-Violence: "Socrates, Jesus, and Martin Luther King
did more for their causes by dying for them than by killing for them."
and
A Message from Peter McWilliams Announcing A Press Conference
And A Statement Of Support From California State Senator Vasconcellos.

After all, the federal government refuses to accept the mandate of California’s voters, who approved the state’s medical marijuana law, Prop. 215, in 1996 by a margin of over 55%.

Again, remember that the tests used by the state cannot distinguish between THC from Marinol and THC from whole cannabis. (Whether the new tests to which McCormick is subjected can detect other cannabinoids is the bone of contention in the Feds efforts to revoke his bail.)
See
September 7th Trial Date Set For McCormick and McWilliams;
McCormick Bail Revocation Hearing Set For March 17.
and
McCormick Now Prisoner Of Pharmaceutical Industry; To Stay Out Of Jail He Must Pay $17,500 To Set Up Test

But this is a California Court, where California – not federal – laws allegedly apply. Brady was accompanied in court by two pro bono attorneys from famed marijuana lawyer Tony Serra’s office. The attorneys pointed out what the Prosecutor already knew- that Brady was a medical marijuana user with a valid recommendation for marijuana -- and a prescription for Marinol. But that didn’t matter to the Prosecutor, who insisted that Brady be urine tested that day.

And -- incredibly -- the judge went along with it.

Although the judge said that Brady was allowed to use medicine prescribed by a doctor, he left open the question about what officers would do if they found medical marijuana in Brady’s possession.

In a case involving another Butte County medical marijuana defendant, Bryan Epis, detectives and the District Attorney’s office were found to have illegally taken confidential attorney-client communication from Epis and used it to violate his constitutional rights.

In the Epis case, as in others, the judge ruled that the DA and police HAD acted totally improperly, but still allowed the case to continue.

The Brady case is also disturbing because police who get to visit and search his home and body at any hour of the day or night are the same police who have been trying to railroad him and extort testimony from him.

"Defendants like Brady can be repeatedly threatened by law enforcement," the local attorney commented. "Police can enter his home without a warrant, search his personal papers, terrorize him, take his medicine, throw him in jail. Under these circumstances, one would hope the court would enjoin such actions, and would protect Brady from retributive prosecution."

Brady says he never thought that the abuses he had written about as a journalist would become so personally familiar to him.

"I am trying to find courage," he said. "This situation has worsened my medical condition and made me fearful for my personal safety. I never felt so vulnerable and alone as I do right now."
